title: Pasqal Demonstrates Hybrid GPU-to-QPU Workflows Using Slurm 26.11 Hierarchical Resources, QRMI, and CUDA-Q - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Pasqal, co-developing with IBM, demonstrated at SC26 a qrmi_hres.lua plugin that lets NVIDIA's Slurm 26.11 Hierarchical Resources framework schedule neutral-atom QPUs (cloud and on-prem, via its Warden middleware) alongside GPUs, replacing license-tracking/SPANK workarounds. Paired with Pulser and CUDA-Q 0.17, it enables dependent pipelines that validate on GPU emulation before triggering runs on physical hardware such as FRESNEL_CAN1 — a sign quantum is being slotted in as a native, schedulable HPC resource.

insights.claim: Pasqal has built an end-to-end quantum-HPC scheduling integration that combines NVIDIA's Slurm 26.11 Hierarchical Resources (HRES) framework with the open-source Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) to manage neutral-atom QPUs alongside classical GPUs, co-developed with IBM and demonstrated at SC26.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum is being integrated into the standard HPC scheduler stack; watch NVIDIA's role as the orchestration layer for hybrid quantum-classical compute.

insights.claim: The Lua-based qrmi_hres.lua Slurm plugin replaces legacy license-tracking and SPANK workarounds previously used to schedule quantum hardware, letting Slurm monitor QPU device availability and schedule jobs across both cloud and on-premises QPUs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removing bespoke integration hacks lowers the cost for supercomputing centers to add QPUs, easing on-prem quantum procurement.
insights.quote: replaces legacy license-tracking and SPANK workarounds

insights.claim: With the Slurm HRES-QRMI integration, HPC administrators can define QPU concurrency limits and maintenance polling intervals directly inside Slurm's resources.yaml configuration file.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QPUs treated as configurable cluster resources signals operational maturity expected by HPC buyers.

insights.claim: For on-premises QPUs protected by Pasqal's open-source Warden middleware, the Slurm controller automatically acquires and revokes user-scoped session tokens via MUNGE authentication, so jobs wait in queue during hardware calibration and release access cleanly on completion or cancellation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Calibration-aware queuing and automated access control address a key operational pain of running QPUs in shared HPC centers.
insights.quote: ensuring jobs wait in queue during hardware calibration and release access cleanly upon completion or cancellation

insights.claim: Pasqal's Slurm scheduling integration builds on production deployments such as the Sol neutral-atom processor installed at Italy's CINECA supercomputing center.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: On-prem installs at European national HPC centers are the proving ground and revenue channel for neutral-atom vendors like Pasqal.
insights.locator: Building on production deployments such as

insights.claim: Pasqal demonstrated multi-stage Slurm batch pipelines pairing its Pulser framework with NVIDIA CUDA-Q 0.17, where a Rydberg-blockade parameter sweep is first validated on a GPU node using CUDA-Q's GPU emulation target (emulate=True) and execution on a physical QPU such as Pasqal's FRESNEL_CAN1 is triggered only if the classical simulation succeeds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GPU emulation acting as a gate before scarce QPU time reinforces GPU demand within quantum workflows and NVIDIA's CUDA-Q lock-in.
insights.quote: automatically trigger execution on a physical processor such as Pasqal’s FRESNEL_CAN1 system only if the classical simulation succeeds
insights.locator: To connect cluster scheduling with application

insights.claim: Slurm 26.11 integration for quantum hardware is becoming a multi-vendor trend at SC26, with Quantum Computing Report also covering Slurm integration briefs for IQM and Alice & Bob, and an IBM-Fermilab-NVIDIA co-design platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Scheduler-level integration is turning into table stakes for QPU vendors selling into HPC; differentiation shifts to hardware performance and uptime.
